A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Oracle-Efficient Combinatorial Semi-Bandits. All 36 pages, including equations, tables, figures, Appendices A.1–A.11, and the checklist, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A.11 report original synthetic experiments measuring regret, oracle usage, and runtime, presented in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A.11 retain the original synthetic experimental results in Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the stated empirical mean by adding division by the observation count. Algorithms 2 and 7 correct cyclic indexing; Algorithms 3–4 correct warm-up pair enumeration to include diagonal pairs. Section 4.2 also shifts Algorithm 4's query grid past warm-up. These are localized procedural corrections within the existing frameworks.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic linear-reward, correlated covariance-adaptive linear-reward, and nonlinear-reward bandit settings in Section 6 and Appendix A.11. No empirical task, domain, or data coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain CUCB in Figure 2, OLS-UCB-C in Figure 3, and SDCB in Figure 4. Citation renumbering and corrections of AROG to AROQ in legends do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported data-generation procedures, arm/cardinality settings, horizons, and regret, runtime, and oracle-complexity measurements are unchanged. Figures 2–4 retain horizons of 20,000, 10,000, and 2,000 rounds, respectively. Algorithm-description corrections do not establish changed experimental execution.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity, robustness, error-analysis, or case-study content is added or removed. Appendix A.11 retains the same supplementary covariance-adaptive and nonlinear-reward benchmark comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same error bars and checklist statement about variation across repeated trials. Neither adds run counts, seeds, an error-bar definition, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 retain the same plotted regret, runtime, oracle adaptivity, and query-complexity results, including error bars and rankings. The experimental findings in Section 6 and Appendix A.11 are unchanged; the legend corrections only repair method names.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds an explicit pair-observability assumption and an extension restricted to observable pairs. Appendix A.5 corrects O(d^2 log(Tm/d)) to O(d^2 log(Tm)); A.6 corrects epoch quantifiers and the induction range, and A.7.1 repairs Equation 6's expected-reward expression. The principal theorem statements and proof strategies remain intact.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects SROQ-C-CMAB's query-complexity claim from Θ(d log log T) to O(d^2 log log T), aligning it with Table 1 and Theorem 4 already present in v1. The central contributions concerning rare oracle queries and regret guarantees remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly explains applicability when some arm pairs cannot co-occur, through restriction to observable pairs. Section 3.2 replaces the stated scheduling regret penalty sqrt(m/log log T) with sqrt(m), and Section 4.2 corrects its query-complexity comparison. Experimental interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 now specifies the exact warm-up offset t_k ← t_k + ceil(d(d+1)/2), and Section 4 supplies observable-pair handling guidance. These improve implementation documentation. The source-code link, experimental data-generation details, and resource disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Tzeng, Ohsaka, and Ariu's Matroid Semi-Bandits in Sublinear Time and explains how its exploitation of matroid structure complements this paper's focus on oracle-call reduction for arbitrary action sets. This is a limited positioning addition.

P1.justification: There are localized paragraph additions, revised stochastic-outcome wording, notation corrections, and consolidation of a duplicate Balkanski–Singer bibliography entry. The main narrative, section order, and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The regret-panel legends in Figures 2–4 correct AROG to AROQ. Expanded prose and pseudocode cause limited page reflow, while the figure panels, axes, table structure, and plotted data remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves internal consistency and algorithm specification by restoring mean normalization, correcting indexing and warm-up descriptions, and aligning covariance-complexity prose with existing formal results. The observable-pair clarification also makes applicability clearer. These are useful localized repairs; the principal theoretical results and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged.
